title: Slice a range
summary: A slice selects a range. Its starting index is included and its stopping index is excluded.
introduction: A slice selects a range. Its starting index is included and its stopping index is excluded. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A slice selects a range. Its starting index is included and its stopping index is excluded.

blocks.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([2, 4, 6, 8])
print(values[1:3].tolist())
blocks.title: Slice a range

blocks.text: The output is [4, 6]. Positions 1 and 2 are selected; position 3 is left out.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Basic slicing often gives a view of the original data, not an independent copy.
For more detail later, use this [NumPy further reading](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/absolute_beginners.html).
